WILLIAMSON COUNTIES                          §       ADMINISTRATIVE HEARINGS


     INTERVENORS JAMIE APPLETON'S. CONRAD APPLETON'S. GRANT
      APPLETON'S, KYMBERLY APPLETON'S, AND RYAN APPLETON'S,
 INDIVIDUALLY AND AS REPRESENTATIVES OF HALL VALLEY ENTERPRISES.
            LLP' S AND MOUNTAIN VALE, LP ' S INITIAL BRIEF

       TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES (ALJ)                                      AND
       COMMISSIONERS OF THE TEXAS PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION:

               COME NOW, Jamie Appleton, Conrad Appleton, Grant Appleton, Kymberly

Appleton, and Ryan Appleton, Individually (the Appletons) and as Representatives ofHall Valley

Enterprises, LLP (Hall Valley) and Mountain Vale, LP (Mountain Vale), Intervenors (SOAH

Order No. 14, Item No. 4679), in the above entitled and numbered matter before the Public Utility

Commission, and files this their Initial Brief pursuant to SOAH Order No. 6 (Item No. 788) after

the week long hearing on the Joint Application of Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC (Oncor)

and LCRA TSC (LCRA) to Amend their Application for a Certificate of Convenience and

Necessity for a Proposed 765-kV Transmission Line from their Bell County East Switch to their

Big Hill Substation (Joint Application). In support oftheir Initial Brief, Intervenors Appleton(s),

Hall Valley, and Mountain Vale would respectfully show that the ALJs and PUC Commission


Appletons' Initial Brief                                            Pagell6
 should deny the Application due to procedural irregularities, prejudicial admission of evidence

favoring the utilities, and the denial oftwo oftheir fellow Intervenors' right to cross-examination,

or alternatively, deny any route near Brady Creek in McCulloch County and within the San Saba

River Basin in McCulloch, Mason and Menard Counties, in particular Links Vl, V3, K52, K61,

K63, L2, M23, M22, Ll, M32, M33, and M8, and would argue the following:

                                          I.      Introduction.

       1.      Intervenors Appleton(s), Hall Valley, and Mountain Vale live and ranch in the rural

counties of McCulloch and San Saba (See Exhibit 1 Conrad Appleton ' s Admitted Direct

Testimony, Appletons 000004) and believe the admitted record shows many deficiencies in the

Joint Application of Oncor and the LCRA that require denial of such. The wide range of evidence

by many of Applicants own witness including their Environmental Assessment (EA), and most of

Intervenors witnesses, identifies significant impacts to the Hill Country environment, agriculture

and ranching operations, livestock, residences, sensitive uses, water resources, cultural and

historical resources, and community values. Most of Applicants' witnesses admitted that their

review of all Route Links was mainly done via desktop or what little could be seen from main

highways. The lack of study of the impact ofthe San Saba River being in the flash flood alley of

Central Texas is quite telling.     Applicants have ignored the devastation that occurred with the

record flood of July 2025 which impact a year later is still being felt by ranchers along the San

Saba. For this deficiency alone, the Joint Application should be denied.

                                  II.    Procedural Deficiencies Noted

       2.      Intervenors Appleton(s), Hall Valley, and Mountain Vale, due to Ryan Appleton

being an attorney at law (See Exhibit 1 Conrad Appleton ' s Admitted Direct Testimony , Appletons




Appletons' Initial Brief                                             Page216
 000004, Paragraph 7), note three major issues that seem to be unfair that would suggest a

procedural bias for the utilities in light of ALJ rulings in the hearing on the merits.

        3.     First, several Intervenors filed Statements or Motions to Conduct a Route

Adequacy Hearing in this matter. (1) 4K Land and Cattle Company's (4K) Statement Challenging

Route Adequacy and their Request for a Hearing on the same (Item No. 3686) ; (2)Burnet County

Commissioner's Court (Burnet) Route Adequacy Challenge and Request for Hearing (Item No.

3679); and (3) Save the Lampasas' (Lampasas) Route Adequacy Challenge (Item No. 3686). It

should be noted several other Intervenors also announced their support for these three route

adequacy challenges. Instead of conducting a hearing as is supposedly provided for by SOAH

Order No. 6, the ALJs summarily ruled with no need for an adequacy hearing. This ruling has

been appealed to the Commission which has placed the item on an upcoming meeting ofthe whole.

       4.       Second, is the admission of Applicants' Exhibit No. 33, a so-called Memo dated

June 10, 2026 (Emphasis added) on the third day of the hearing on the merits to Governor Greg

Abbott and others from the Texas Oil & Gas Association, Permian Basin Petroleum Association,

Texas Alliance of Energy Producers, Texas Independent Producers & Royalty Owners

Association, and the Texas Pipeline Association, none of whom were parties to this proceeding.

Applicant LCRA's counsel sneakily asked the Staffs expert witness John Poole, P.E., on that very

day June 10, 2026, if he had seen the Memo without showing it on a screen or allowing any time

for all other parties to have the opportunity to see, reflect upon, and formulate any objections to

Applicants' Exhibit 33. The Exhibit was not sponsored by its author (who was never identified)

nor by any recipient to whom the Memo was addressed. Authentication is therefore totally lacking

and was never produced by Applicants prior to the morning ofJune 10 in the middle ofthe hearing

on the merits. Exhibit 33 is nothing more than a hearsay document adding Direct Testimony by



Appletons' Initial Brief                                               Page316
 an unknown author whose knowledge of the facts asserted in the Memo cannot be tested by cross-

examination. It unfairly prohibits Intervenors from designating the author of the Memo for cross-

examination on their own witness lists. Exhibit 33 should be stricken from the record for unfair

trial tactics and lack of evidentiary basis.

        5.      Third, id the refusal to allow fellow McCulloch County Intervenors Bruce James

and Gerald Nobles to cross-exam each other that they apparently had properly designated on their

cross-examination witness list. Few rights in the trial of contested matters are more sacred than

the right to cross-exam other witnesses whether they are friendly or not. The ALJs had already

imposed a three (3) minute time limit on Intervenors cross-examination of witnesses. The ALJs

had also announced the daily time for the hearing to be over was 5:00 PM. The denial of these

Intervenors, the last two witnesses to be called in this matter, to cross-examine each other when

viewed with the ALJs allowance ofnew evidence to be submitted by Applicants (Exhibit 33) again

suggests a procedural bias for the utilities in light of ALJs' rulings. Intervenors Appleton(s), Hall

Valley, and Mountain Vale have reviewed Reata' s and L Bar' s Motion to Reconsider and Offer of

Proof (Item No. 6138) and incorporate by reference their legal arguments herein.

                                III.    Needs and Route Arguments

        6.      As clearly gleaned from the totality of the hearing on the merits, transmission lines

do not generate electricity. The proposed first ofits kind in Texas 765-kV facilities running through

Bell, Burnet, Concho, Coryell, Lampasas, Llano, Mason, McCulloch, Menard, Milam, Mills, San

Saba, Schleicher, Tom Green, and Williamson Counties would transport power, but it would not

add generation capacity to the ERCOT system or create new supply for the Permian Basin. Nor

would this new line provide the citizens of these counties with electricity, only a memory of what




Appletons' Initial Brief                                              Page416
 their land used to look like. So Applicants Joint Application simply won't solve the problem of

providing Texans with more reliable or less expensive energy.

       7.. a. any witnesses pointed out by placing reliable, economical natural gas generating

power plants in and around the Permian Basin which would be closer to the claimed demand for

electricity, should achieve Texas's energy reliability needs with fewer Hill Country land-use

impacts and ultimately and more importantly, lower costs to ratepayers. We would argue to deny

this Joint Application and seek to add natural gas generation in West Texas. This would then

reduce or eliminate the need for the 765-kV transmission lines destroying the beauty, heritage,

historical and cultural values ofthe Hill Country of Texas.

       8.      In light of the serious irregularities in this proceeding noted above, the May 11,

2026, letter to the Commission from some 25 Texas Legislators expressing their concern that this

proceeding exceeds the limited scope of HB 5066 (Item No, 4620, and now the Amicus Brief and

Motion to Defer the needs issue from some 34 Texas House Members and 9 Texas Senate

Members (Item No. 6139), this proceeding should be stopped and either deferred or denied without

prejudice after further study is conducted. See also Direct Testimony of former Chairman of the

PUC Barry T, Smitherman (Item No, 4334).

       9.      Alternatively, with regard to the Rote structure if the ALJs and Commissioners

insist on ignoring the above, the most compelling testimony from McCulloch County was from J.

Luther King, the largest landowner in McCulloch County, with a lifetime of boots on the ground

knowledge of the best terrain on which to build a transmission line project as suggested is needed

by Oncor and LCRA. (Items Nos. 4440 and 5026). That is the Norther Route through McCulloch

County staying as far away from the San Saba River and Flash Flood Alley.         See also Expert

Testimony of James E. Scott, III (Item Nos. 4507 and 5086).



Appletons' Initial Brief                                            Page516
        WHEREFORE, PREMISES CONSIDERED, Intervenors Appleton(s), Hall Valley, and

Mountain Vale respectfully request that the ALJs and Commissioners take Notice of their Initial

Brief after the hearing on the Merits in this matter, deny the Joint Application of Oncor and LCRA,

or at least defer such decision in accordance with the comments of our Texas Legislators, or if a

rote is determined to be necessary, at least for McCulloch County, avoid all routes impacting the

San Saba River and Brady Creek, follow the suggestions of J. Luther King and James E. Scott, III,

and for such other relief to which they are justly entitled.
